knowledge:
- key_parameters: sample_dir=The directory containing the input files generated by the scIGD workflow ;; filter_mode=The cell filtering mode, which can be "no" (default, filters out cells with 0 counts), "yes" (advanced filtering based on the knee plot inflection point), or "custom" (filters based on a user-defined threshold) ;; lookup_file=A CSV file or data frame mapping alleles to genes and functional classes ;; barcode_file=The file name containing cell barcodes ;; gene_file=The file name containing feature identifiers ;; matrix_file=The file name containing the quantification matrix ;; log=Logical indicating whether to compute a logcounts assay using library factors (default is TRUE) ;; gene_symbols=Logical indicating whether to compute additional gene symbols using org.Hs.eg.db if raw data only has Ensembl IDs (default is FALSE)
- alternatives: Standard single-cell analysis packages like scater, scran, scuttle, and DropletUtils are used for downstream analysis, but SingleCellAlleleExperiment is uniquely required to handle the multi-layer allele-aware data structure.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing single-cell RNA-sequencing data (e.g., 10x or BD Rhapsody) where allele-specific and functional-level quantification of highly polymorphic immune genes (HLAs, KIRs, Igs) is required.
- pitfalls: If computing scaling factors/logcounts manually (not using log=TRUE during read-in), scaling factors must only be computed on data layers present in the raw data (non-immune and alleles) to avoid incorrect scaling due to the aggregated layers ;; filter_mode="yes" requires the DropletUtils package to be installed ;; When running dimensionality reduction (like PCA or t-SNE) on different layers, unique names (e.g., name="PCA_a", name="PCA_g") must be specified to prevent overwriting the default "PCA" slot.

workflows.name: allele_aware_single_cell_analysis
workflows.intent: Read allele-level single-cell quantification data, aggregate it into gene and functional layers, filter cells, and perform layer-specific dimensionality reduction.
input: lookup_table.csv (mapping of alleles to genes and functional classes)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the lookup table mapping alleles to genes and functions ;; 2. Read raw allele counts and construct the SingleCellAlleleExperiment object using read_allele_counts(), applying knee-plot or custom filtering ;; 3. Subset the dataset into specific layers (non-immune, alleles, immune genes, functional groups) using scae_subset() ;; 4. Model gene variance and identify highly variable genes (HVGs) for each layer using modelGeneVar() and getTopHVGs() ;; 5. Run PCA on each layer using runPCA() with unique names to avoid overwriting ;; 6. Run t-SNE on the reduced dimensions using runTSNE() ;; 7. Plot expression and reduced dimensions using plotExpression() and plotReducedDim()
workflows.code:
lookup_name <- "pbmc_10k_lookup_table.csv"
lookup <- utils::read.csv(system.file("extdata", lookup_name, package="scaeData"))

scae <- read_allele_counts(example_data_10k$dir,
                           sample_names="example_data",
                           filter_mode="yes",
                           lookup_file=lookup,
                           barcode_file=example_data_10k$barcodes,
                           gene_file=example_data_10k$features,
                           matrix_file=example_data_10k$matrix,
                           log=TRUE)

scae_nonimmune_subset <- scae_subset(scae, "nonimmune")
scae_alleles_subset <- scae_subset(scae, "alleles")
scae_immune_genes_subset <- scae_subset(scae, "immune_genes")
scae_functional_groups_subset <- scae_subset(scae, "functional_groups")

rn_scae_ni <- rownames(scae_subset(scae, "nonimmune"))
rn_scae_alleles <- rownames(scae_subset(scae, "alleles"))

scae_nonimmune__allels_subset <- scae[c(rn_scae_ni, rn_scae_alleles), ]

rn_scae_i <- rownames(scae_subset(scae, "immune_genes"))

scae_nonimmune__immune <- scae[c(rn_scae_ni, rn_scae_i), ]

rn_scae_functional <- rownames(scae_subset(scae, "functional_groups"))

scae_nonimmune__functional <- scae[c(rn_scae_ni, rn_scae_functional), ]

df_ni_a <- modelGeneVar(scae_nonimmune__allels_subset)
top_ni_a <- getTopHVGs(df_ni_a, prop=0.1)

df_ni_g <- modelGeneVar(scae_nonimmune__immune)
top_ni_g <- getTopHVGs(df_ni_g, prop=0.1)

df_ni_f <- modelGeneVar(scae_nonimmune__functional)
top_ni_f <- getTopHVGs(df_ni_f, prop=0.1)

assay <- "logcounts"

scae <- runPCA(scae, ncomponents=10, subset_row=top_ni_a,
               exprs_values=assay, name="PCA_a")

scae <- runPCA(scae, ncomponents=10, subset_row=top_ni_g,
               exprs_values=assay, name="PCA_g")

scae <- runPCA(scae, ncomponents=10, subset_row=top_ni_f,
               exprs_values=assay, name="PCA_f")

set.seed(18)
scae <- runTSNE(scae, dimred="PCA_g",  name="TSNE_g")

tsne <- "TSNE_g"

tsne_g_a  <- plotReducedDim(scae, dimred=tsne, colour_by="HLA-DRB1") +
             ggtitle("HLA-DRB1 gene")

tsne_g_a1 <- plotReducedDim(scae, dimred=tsne, colour_by="DRB1*07:01:01:01") + 
             ggtitle("Allele DRB1*07:01:01:01")

tsne_g_a2 <- plotReducedDim(scae, dimred=tsne, colour_by="DRB1*13:01:01:01") + 
             ggtitle("Allele DRB1*13:01:01:01")

p2 <- tsne_g_a + tsne_g_a1 + tsne_g_a2
